Why go: Ang Thong Marine Park by big boat

Ang Thong National Marine Park is a chain of 42 limestone islands about 30 km west of Koh Samui, protected since 1980 and covering about 102 km² of sea and land. The highlights are the same on every Ang Thong day trip: the Emerald Lake (Thale Nai), a cliff-ringed saltwater lagoon on Koh Mae Ko seen from a platform at the top of 15–20 minutes of wooden steps, and the viewpoint above the park headquarters on Koh Wua Talab (Wua Ta Lap), reached by a steep 500 m trail with ropes near the top. In between come kayaking and snorkelling around the smaller islands.

What changes on the big boat is the ride. A larger hull moves less in swell than a speedboat, you sit in the shade with room to stand up and walk around, and spray is not a factor. The crossing is slower, about 1.5 hours each way against roughly an hour by speedboat, so the day is longer: about 10 hours door to door, with the boat back at the pier around 18:00 and hotel drop-off between 18:00 and 19:00. You see the same places for 1,500 THB, 300 THB less than the speedboat, but you spend more of the day travelling.

Lunch is a Thai buffet with rice, several hot dishes and fresh fruit, with vegetarian dishes always available. The day suits people who would rather sit on a steady deck with the islands going past than hold on through a fast, bumpy crossing.

Who this tour is for

  • Anyone who gets seasick on small boats: the big boat is the steadiest way to reach Ang Thong.
  • Families with younger children, who have space to move and shade on deck. Children aged 3–11 pay the child price and infants up to 2 travel free.
  • Older travellers and guests with back or neck problems who want to avoid the speedboat's bouncing.
  • Travellers on a budget: it is our lowest Ang Thong price.

Who should choose another tour

  • Short on time or want more time in the park: the speedboat tour is back about two hours earlier.
  • Want a quieter, more personal day: the VIP tour takes only 15 guests on a big speedboat.
  • Need your own schedule: the private speedboat.
  • Want a short, easy half day instead: the Pig Island speedboat tour is 4–5 hours with a crossing of under 30 minutes.
  • Travelling 1 November–15 December: the park is closed; see the Koh Tao day trip or Pig Island.

What to bring

  • Cash for the park fee: 300 THB per foreign adult, 150 THB per child aged 3–14 (under-3s free). Thai baht only.
  • Swimwear, a towel and a change of clothes.
  • Reef-safe sunscreen, a hat and sunglasses.
  • A light long-sleeved layer: the open deck is windy on the way home.
  • Shoes with grip for the stairs and the viewpoint trail.
  • A dry bag or phone pouch for kayaking.
  • Seasickness tablets if you are very sensitive; it is still an open-sea crossing.
  • Your passport number for the booking (accident insurance).

Good to know

  • Season: closed every year 1 November–15 December, reopening 16 December. February to April is calmest; May to September is good most days; October is wetter. December to February is peak season with park quotas, so book early.
  • Weather: rain alone does not cancel the trip; strong wind and waves do. If the captain cancels for safety we tell you the evening before, and you choose a full refund or a new date. Forecasts: windy.com and our sea conditions page.
  • Seasickness: sit in the middle of the boat, low down and in fresh air. Avoid reading or watching your phone on the crossing.
  • Pregnancy: the big boat is the gentlest Ang Thong option, but the crossing is open sea and the boarding and stairs need care. Ask your doctor and message us before booking.
  • Mobility: boarding uses a gangway or steps, and both viewpoints are optional. Guests can stay on the beach at Koh Wua Talab while others climb.
  • Sun: shade on deck helps, but kayaking and beach time are in full sun. Reapply sunscreen after every swim.
  • Children: children's life jackets are always on board and children wear them at all times on the boat.
  • Park rules: no swimming in the Emerald Lake, no fires, no feeding monkeys, no touching coral, and all rubbish goes back on the boat. Sunscreens with oxybenzone, octinoxate, 4-MBC or butylparaben are banned in Thai marine national parks.
  • Drones: need prior Department of National Parks permission and CAAT/NBTC registration; otherwise don't bring one.

Pickup and meeting point

Hotel transfers are included from the main areas of Koh Samui: Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut, Maenam, Choeng Mon, Bang Rak and Plai Laem. Remote areas (Nathon, Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao, Thong Krut and similar) cost 400 THB per person return, added on the booking card. Pickup is 07:30–08:30 and check-in at the pier is 08:30–08:45, with a life-jacket fitting and safety briefing. We send your exact time and the pier location by email and WhatsApp the day before. You are also welcome to meet the boat at the pier.
